note: Two publications, two thresholds, one deliberate hole. The eras are kept separate on purpose: the disclosure threshold moved from £150,000 to £174,000 between the 2022 and 2025 editions, and no list was published for 30 September 2023 or 30 September 2024. Nothing here is interpolated across that hole. Individual names are published upstream under OGL and are deliberately not republished: this file carries counts, bands, job titles, organisation and grade only.

series.note: Counted against the threshold this publication was published at (earning £150,000 and above).

series.label: Cabinet Office senior officials' 'high earners' list — Civil Service only
series.note: Counted against the threshold this publication was published at (earning more than £174,000).

series.label: 2010-2022 recounted at the £174,000 cutoff — Civil Service only
series.note: Derived, not published. The 2010-2022 files list everyone at or above £150,000, so recounting them at £174,000 gives a like-for-like line against the 2025 list. It is a range because £174,000 falls inside the published £170,000-£174,999 band. It is NOT a published statistic and must never be drawn as one line with the published series.

series.label: 2010-2022 recounted at the £174,000 cutoff — all published organisations
series.note: Derived, not published. The 2010-2022 files list everyone at or above £150,000, so recounting them at £174,000 gives a like-for-like line against the 2025 list. It is a range because £174,000 falls inside the published £170,000-£174,999 band. It is NOT a published statistic and must never be drawn as one line with the published series.

gaps.reason: No high-earner list was published for these dates. The 2010-2022 publication was frozen and the replacement publication begins at 30 September 2025. The threshold also changed across this gap, so the two ends are not the same measurement.

breaks.note: Disclosure threshold raised from £150,000 to £174,000, matching HM Treasury senior pay approval guidance. The list gets shorter for that reason alone.
First edition to publish "Type of organisation". Before it, civil service and public-sector-commercial rows cannot be told apart, so no civil-service series exists for the earlier editions.
Reference date moved from 31 March (150k-2014-03-31) to 30 September (150k-2015-09-30). Consecutive editions across that move are 18 months apart, not 12.
These editions state a year and no reference date. None is inferred: they are plotted by year and should be drawn as such.
